faq.a: The earliest alphabet was made around 1800 BCE by Semitic-speaking workers in Egypt and Sinai, who used Egyptian pictures to stand for single sounds. The Phoenicians later spread it widely.

faq.q: Who added vowels to the alphabet?
faq.a: The Greeks, around 800 BCE. The Phoenician alphabet had only consonants, so the Greeks used some spare letters for vowel sounds.

faq.q: Why is it called the alphabet?
faq.a: It comes from alpha and beta, the first two letters of the Greek alphabet. In the same way, some people say ABC.
asks: Where does the word alphabet come from?

faq.q: Where does the letter A come from?
faq.a: A comes from a picture of an ox head, called aleph. Turn a capital A upside down and you can still see the head and horns.

faq.q: Is the alphabet the only way to write?
faq.a: No. Chinese uses characters for words and syllables, Japanese kana stand for syllables, and Devanagari joins consonants and vowels in syllable blocks.

facts: The Phoenician alphabet had 22 letters, all for consonant sounds.
The word alphabet comes from alpha and beta, the first two Greek letters.
The Latin alphabet is the most widely used writing system in the world.
